attestations.name: HIPAA-ready configuration (BAA available)
attestations.scope: Eligible orgs review/execute the BAA and enable HIPAA readiness in the Claude Console

implements.summary: Workspace and active API-key inventory read from the Admin API; required workspaces asserted to exist; workspaces created idempotently by name.

Key hygiene — active-key count threshold, stale-key (age) and no-expiry detection, no personal keys in service-account-only workspaces; stale keys disabled via status "inactive"; members added with least-privilege workspace roles. Workload Identity Federation (AWS, GitHub Actions, Google Cloud, Kubernetes, Entra ID, Okta, SPIFFE) is the recommended replacement for static keys.
Inference and storage geography made explicit per workspace and per request; usage reports grouped by inference_geo provide transfer evidence.
Compliance API Activity Feed (GET /v1/compliance/activities, retained 6 years) exported to JSONL for the SIEM; usage and cost reports exported.
Workloads kept out of the Default Workspace (where spend/rate limits cannot be set) and required workspaces verified to have rate-limit overrides; workspace spend limits set in the Console.

gaps.note: No organization- or workspace-level model allow-list was found in the Admin API documentation (verified 2026-10-13). Enforce approved models in an API gateway or application config, or consume Claude via a cloud that has model-access policy (Vertex vertexai.allowedModels, Azure 'Foundry model deployments should only use approved models', Bedrock SCP on foundation-model ARNs).

Runtime guardrails and content filtering are the customer's responsibility on the first-party API. When Claude is consumed via Bedrock, Vertex AI or Microsoft Foundry, use those platforms' guardrails (Bedrock Guardrails, Model Armor, Azure content filters) — see the cloud packs.

API keys cannot be created through the Admin API (Console only); the API exposes created_at/expires_at but no last-used time, so staleness is approximated by age. Workspace spend and rate limits can only be written in the Console.

Workspace spend limits cannot be read or set through the documented Admin API for Console orgs (Spend Limits API is Claude Enterprise only); rate-limit overrides are readable but written in the Console. The Default Workspace cannot carry limits at all.
Workspace geo is 'us' only; there is no in-region storage for EU/AU/NZ on the first-party API — document the transfer mechanism (DPA/SCCs) or use a hyperscaler region.
CMEK (external_key_id via the External Keys API; AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS) exists but is not configured by this pack; eligibility per organization.
SCIM is documented for the Enterprise plan only (Team plan UNVERIFIED); IdP groups do not map to Claude roles.

No private network path to api.anthropic.com and workspace storage geo is currently US only; for NZ, AU, EU and LatAm users the first-party API is a cross-border transfer (see AIG-18), not network isolation. Consume Claude through Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry when private endpoints and in-region storage are required.

Personal-data protection is contractual and configurational rather than code: conversation content is not retained by default (Covered Models 30 days), ZDR is arranged through sales, and HIPAA readiness/BAA is enabled in the Console. Evidence these in the system record; PII filtering must be implemented in the application or the hosting cloud's guardrails.

attestations.name: AWS Audit Manager: AWS Generative AI Best Practices Framework v2
attestations.scope: Prebuilt assessment framework (72 automated and 38 manual controls, 8 control sets) covering Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI. Evidence tooling, not a certification. Audit Manager is no longer open to new customers.

implements.summary: Guardrail sensitive-information filters anonymise EMAIL, PHONE, NAME and ADDRESS and block card numbers, CVVs, passwords and AWS keys on input and output; extra PII types and regexes are variables.
SCP denies InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream (which also covers Converse and StartAsyncInvoke) on every foundation model and inference profile not in the approved list.

SCP condition on bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier makes every InvokeModel/Converse call name the approved guardrail ARN:version; the log-delivery role trusts only bedrock.amazonaws.com for this account and Region and can write only the invocation log stream; an optional SCP lets only named admin roles change invocation logging.

Interface VPC endpoints with private DNS for bedrock, bedrock-runtime and bedrock-agent-runtime; SCP denies Bedrock calls outside approved Regions (aws:RequestedRegion) and, unless allowed, global cross-Region inference.
Optional customer managed KMS keys for the guardrail (kms_key_arn), the invocation-log bucket (SSE-KMS) and the log group; SSE-S3 and a TLS-only bucket policy otherwise.

Baseline guardrail (HATE, INSULTS, SEXUAL, VIOLENCE, MISCONDUCT at HIGH; PROMPT_ATTACK at HIGH on input; denied topics; managed profanity list; grounding and relevance at 0.75) with a numbered version, enforced organization-wide through BEDROCK_POLICY and account-wide through EnforcedGuardrailConfiguration.

Model invocation logging (off by default) to CloudWatch Logs with 400-day retention and to a versioned, private S3 bucket that also holds payloads over 100 KB. InvokeModel and Converse are CloudTrail management events (logged by default); agent, knowledge-base, flow and ApplyGuardrail calls are data events that must be enabled separately in CloudTrail.
Guardrail changes produce a new, immutable numbered version; old versions are retained for audit and rollback, and enforcement always references a numbered version, never DRAFT.

gaps.note: This pack does not build an inventory. Bedrock has no single AI-asset inventory; combine AWS Config resource recording for AWS::Bedrock::* types, invocation logs (which model each workload calls) and the repository's AI system records under mlops/.

Automated Reasoning checks have no argument in aws_bedrock_guardrail (CloudFormation has AutomatedReasoningPolicyConfig), and guardrails that use Automated Reasoning cannot be enforced. No Terraform resource for account-level enforcement (PutEnforcedGuardrailConfiguration) was found; use the CloudFormation template.

The bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier condition applies to InvokeModel, InvokeModelWithResponseStream, Converse and ConverseStream only. RetrieveAndGenerate, InvokeAgent and InvokeInlineAgent need their own guardrail configuration, and input tags let callers limit which prompt content is evaluated. BEDROCK_POLICY enforcement covers those gaps for the Regions it lists.

AWS Config has no managed rule for "guardrail attached" or "invocation logging enabled"; the only Bedrock managed rules cover data-source and AgentCore settings. Detect drift with a custom Config rule or with the SCP that protects the logging configuration. Invocation logging covers bedrock-runtime only, not bedrock-mantle.
Human oversight is an application and process control; Bedrock provides no platform enforcement.

AI disclosure, explanation and synthetic-content marking are application responsibilities.

Training is organisational.

UNVERIFIED whether constraints/gcp.resourceLocations limits where online inference on publisher models is processed (for example via the global endpoint). Pin regional endpoints in clients.

Not covered. Security Command Center AI Protection (Premium/Enterprise) provides AI asset inventory and the "Google Recommended AI Essentials - Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform" Compliance Manager framework; the SCC Enterprise tier shuts down on 2027-05-21.

implements.summary: Approved Llama models enforced per host — Vertex AI vertexai.allowedModels org policy, Azure built-in policy aafe3651-cb78-4f68-9f81-e7e41509110f (approved publishers/asset IDs), Bedrock SCP denying non-approved foundation-model ARNs; Llama 4 license obligations (700M MAU, AUP, EU multimodal restriction, derived-model naming) tracked as a checklist.

Llama Guard 4 hazard policy (S1–S14, block/flag per category, fail closed), Prompt Guard 2 for injection/jailbreak, LlamaFirewall input gate, and OGX >= 1.0 moderation via an OpenAI-compatible /v1/moderations endpoint.

gaps.note: Self-hosted Llama has no vendor logging: prompt/response, guardrail-decision and access logging are the operator's responsibility (gateway / inference-server logs to the SIEM). Hosted Llama uses the cloud's logging (Bedrock invocation logging is off by default; Vertex Data Access logs are off by default) — see the cloud packs.
Self-hosted inference endpoints have no built-in identity: front them with workload identity, mTLS and per-agent authorization (see the zero-trust controls).
Network isolation for self-hosted Llama is the operator's responsibility (private subnets, no public endpoint, egress control); for hosted Llama use the cloud's private endpoints.

Exact Llama 4 model IDs per cloud (Vertex model names, Foundry publisher/asset IDs, Bedrock meta.* model IDs) were not verified from cloud docs in this pass — copy them from each model catalog. Model-weight integrity (hash/signature checks on downloaded weights) must be enforced in the MLOps pipeline.

Hosted-cloud default content filters for Llama (Bedrock Guardrails, Azure AI Content Safety, Model Armor) are UNVERIFIED for Llama specifically; apply the cloud packs' guardrails explicitly. OGX >= 1.0 has no shields API.

CyberSecEval 4 is a benchmark suite, not a control this pack automates; run it in your evaluation pipeline and record the result in testing.evaluation_completed / red_team_completed. llamafirewall_gate.py is a runtime input gate (AIG-10), not a test harness.
Attribution ('Built with Llama', 'Llama' naming prefix, NOTICE file) is a licence obligation evidenced by the checklist in native/license-compliance.yaml; nothing in this pack enforces it at runtime.

Project data-retention override (default inherits the organization policy; ZDR / MAM and enhanced variants once OpenAI has approved them). API data is not used for training by default.

Audit logs (user actions and configuration changes) are exported from GET /v1/organization/audit_logs to JSONL for the SIEM; spend alerts notify the platform team.

Hard monthly spend limits (project and optional organization) return 429 once reached and act as a blast-radius control; spend alerts fire first; project rate limits cap request and token volume per approved model.

gaps.note: API-key scopes and restricted-key permissions are not managed by the Terraform provider (keys are created through the Admin API, the value is returned once). SCIM for API Platform orgs is UNVERIFIED. Enforce key rotation and storage in your secrets manager.
Customer-managed keys: openai_project exposes `external_key_id`, but CMK enrolment requirements were not verified; not enabled by this pack.
No org-wide enforced moderation: the Moderation API is opt-in per request; the application must call it (or use inline moderation on Responses) and act on the result.

Audit logs cover administrative actions, not prompt/response content. Whether audit logging must be enabled first and its retention period are UNVERIFIED. Prompt/response logging is the application's responsibility (and conflicts with ZDR).

ZDR, MAM and their enhanced variants require prior OpenAI approval; endpoints that keep state (assistants, threads, vector_stores, files, fine_tuning, evals, batches) are not ZDR-eligible — block them in the application if ZDR is required.
Human oversight is an application-level design control; the platform has no native approval workflow.

No private network path to api.openai.com. Data residency is a sales-gated project option with regional prefixes (e.g. eu.api.openai.com); it controls where data is stored/processed, not network isolation. Treat residency under AIG-18.
